title: Health Legislation Amendment (Improved Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2018
short_title: Health Legislation Amendment (Improved Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill would help the government recover more money that was overpaid to health practitioners through Medicare and related schemes.
It would give the government stronger tools to take money from future payments to practitioners who owe debts, and standardise record-keeping rules for doctors, pharmacists and dentists.
From July 2019, large practices and corporations that bill on behalf of practitioners could also be held responsible for repaying incorrect claims.
changes: Strengthens the government's ability to recover Medicare debts by allowing it to redirect future bulk-billed payments and garnish other funds owed to practitioners.
Makes the rules for keeping and providing documents the same for all health professionals under the three main health payment schemes.
Introduces a Shared Debt Recovery Scheme from 1 July 2019 that can make employers and corporate entities jointly liable for repaying debts.
summary.affected: Medical practitioners, pharmacists, dentists, and the corporate entities or employers that bill on their behalf.

speeches.speaker: Greg Hunt
speeches.brief: The Health Legislation Amendment (Improved Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2018 was introduced to implement 2017 budget measures improving Medicare debt recovery, saving $103.8 million over four years for reinvestment. It allows offsetting or garnishee of up to 20% of future bulk-billed claims for practitioners with proven incorrect claims who refuse repayment plans, extends Professional Services Review jurisdiction to corporate medical practices with contractors, and introduces shared debt recovery for practitioners and employers from 1 July 2019, supported by the Australian Medical Association and the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners.

speeches.speaker: Catherine King
speeches.brief: The Health Legislation Amendment (Improved Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2018 amends three acts to improve Medicare compliance and debt recovery, with estimated savings of $103 million. Labor supports the bill but argues the government cannot be trusted with Medicare, citing outstanding debts of over $50 million and only 40% recovery.

speeches.speaker: Emma McBride
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Health Legislation Amendment (Improved Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2018 and an amendment by the member for Ballarat, noting it would save $103 million by improving Medicare compliance and debt recovery, with only 40% of debts recovered and over $50 million outstanding. The speaker also criticised the government’s Medicare rebate freeze and rising out-of-pocket costs, citing average GP fees of $38.44 and specialist fees of $87.62 in early 2018, and announced Labor’s commitment to new MRI licence investments.

speeches.speaker: Greg Hunt
speeches.brief: The Health Legislation Amendment (Improved Medicare Compliance and Other Measures) Bill 2018 implements 2017 budget measures to strengthen Medicare integrity, supported by record funding and a 3.8% increase in bulk-billing since the government took office. The bill allows reducing future bulk-billed claims by up to 20% or garnisheeing other funds to recover overpayments, and makes employers jointly liable for debts, with additional safeguards for doctors after consultation with the Australian Medical Association and the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners.
